items.key: ai:the gandhi photograph you carry in your wallet: who actually took it and how did it end up on indian currency notes?
items.text: The Gandhi Photograph You Carry In Your Wallet: Who Actually Took It And How Did It End Up On Indian Currency Notes?
items.article: This Gandhi Jayanti, look closely at your Rs 500 note. The famous face on your currency note wasn’t drawn Every day, over a billion people handle Indian currency notes featuring the smiling portrait of Mahatma Gandhi. Yet, despite its presence in almost every wallet across the nation, few know the origins of this iconic image. Contrary to common belief, the portrait is neither an artistic drawing nor an official state portrait. It is a cropped, mirrored section of an authentic photograph taken during a pivotal political meeting in Delhi in 1946. The original photograph was captured outside Viceregal House, now known as Rashtrapati Bhavan, in Delhi. Mahatma Gandhi was attending crucial political negotiations regarding the transfer of power alongside British diplomat Lord Frederick William Pethick-Lawrence. In the original full-length frame, Gandhi is seen standing next to Lord Pethick-Lawrence, sharing a candid, warm smile. The identity of the photographer remains disputed among historical archivists, though many attribute the historic shot to an unknown press photographer working for the British colonial administration. When the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) selected the image for currency design, security designers executed a subtle transformation. Designers cropped Lord Pethick-Lawrence out of the frame entirely, isolating Gandhi’s face and shoulders. There comes a time in every avid reader’s life when they must put away serious things and take up more (im)mature ones. Rebecca Yarros’ Fourth Wing was the first novel to shift my perspective on the BookTok-dubbed genre of ‘romantasy’. While I’m not hailing it as a piece of prized literature, I can safely declare it to be an enthralling book with well-developed characters and the perfect balance of romance and fantasy. Chances are you agree, or else you wouldn’t have landed on this article. Yarros’ latest instalment, Threshing Day , was released on 29 September – and if you’ve already torn through its 13 stories, you’re in the right place. Beyond plotting, betrayal, and cold-blooded murder, the rugged, romantic Scottish landscape steals the show in The Traitors. Filmed at Ardross Castle, the privately owned historic property is as much a main character as presenter Claudia Winkleman ( and her coat collection ). Built in the Scottish Baronial style, the 19th-century estate is spread across 100 acres of parkland, north of Inverness along the River Alness. Its imposing facade, grand staircases and turrets set the moody tone of the TV show. Beyond the castle, shots of misty glens, brooding skies and forest wildernesses have increasingly put Scotland on the tourism map. Since the first series of The Traitors aired in 2022, the show has delivered an estimated £21.8 million boost to the Scottish economy, according to the BBC’s economic impact report.

items.article: Scotland is renowned for its Highland cows, whose long horns and shaggy coats attract visitors from around the world. Published: 18:21, 2 October 2026 | Updated: 18:23, 2 October 2026 But it is an endangered breed of Irish cattle that been harnessed to restore the country’s struggling rainforests. A dozen heads of Droimeann cattle have arrived Ardtornish Estate, in the Morvern Peninsula, Argyllshire, where they will be put to work across woodland, scrub and rough grazing. It is the first time in centuries the cows have been brought over. They will now be put to work across woodland, scrub and rough grazing for the West Highland rainforest renewal project. The role of the ancient breed is to break up dense bracken, manage coarse grasses and help establish the conditions for a wider range of plants and habitats to recover, while being the start of a working herd that can produce food.

Whether it's a pair of nail scissors, a razor or an extra power bank that has you receiving that oh-so-judgemental look from security personnel, it's always frustrating to have your belongings confiscated before jetting off on holiday. Earlier this year, Manchester Airport showcased a selection of items its security officers were forced to confiscate in the space of just one morning. items.article: CASES of aggressive bowel cancer that kills half of those it strikes are rising in teens and young adults, scientists warn. As the disease... CASES of aggressive bowel cancer that kills half of those it strikes are rising in teens and young adults, scientists warn. As the disease historically affects older adults, youngsters may be missing warning signs – which include tummy aches and lower back pain. Researchers from Mass General Brigham for Children and Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute found that children and teens with bowel cancer face “extreme delays” in diagnosis. As a result, many won’t be diagnosed with cancer until it’s reached an advanced stage – making treatment trickier and increasing the likelihood of death. items.text: The truth behind your menopause supplements: How the health industry is preying on midlife women with HRT alternatives, exposed by doctor and broadcaster XAND VAN TULLEKEN
items.article: Are you a woman worried about the menopause? There's a supplement for that. Dozens, in fact - as well as menopause shampoo, menopause face cream and even menopause chocolate. Published: 01:00, 7 September 2026 | Updated: 09:24, 7 September 2026 Dr Xand van Tulleken previously exposed the truth about celebrity-endorsed supplements that claim to promote longevity . Now, he delves into the booming menopause industry and reveals the damaging role social media plays in the promotion of wellness. Are you a woman worried about the menopause ? There’s a supplement for that. Dozens, in fact – as well as menopause shampoo, menopause face cream, menopause clothes… and even menopause chocolate. How did the menopause create such a booming industry? The answer goes back almost a quarter of a century to 2002, when part of a major HRT trial was stopped early. The headline finding was a 26 per cent increase in invasive breast cancer in the women taking combined oestrogen and progestin – the standard HRT – compared with those on placebo. The trial had also found increases in heart attack, stroke and blood clots, partly offset by fewer hip fractures and cases of colon cancer. The study was later found to be flawed – the actual increased risk was a tiny 0.5 per cent – but it kick-started a major panic among women with the result that many either stopped taking HRT or decided to avoid it altogether.

items.text: The truth behind the wellness industry's dubious promises: From the watch that could do you more harm than good to vitamin drips loved by celebrities, XAND VAN TULLEKEN exposes the products that simply prey on your health anxieties
items.article: There is a fundamental difficulty facing anyone who wants to increase human lifespan. It is that our bodies aren't built to last. Published: 01:01, 6 September 2026 | Updated: 10:24, 6 September 2026 Doctor and broadcaster XAND VAN TULLEKEN yesterday revealed how faddy multivitamins make little difference to our health. Today, continuing his excoriating denunciation of the wellness industry, he explains why eternal youth is a dangerous (and expensive) myth... There is a fundamental difficulty facing anyone who wants to increase human lifespan. It is that our bodies aren’t built to last. Whereas healthcare has limited ambitions – it wants to stop us falling through the floor – the wellness industry is about raising the ceiling. And since the idea of being dead is hard to wrap our heads around, longevity is an easy sell. Having trained as a doctor and worked as a broadcaster for 20 years, my new book is part of an attempt to understand the wellness industry – by exploring in-depth supplements, wearable tech and testing. Longevity is such an attractive concept for marketing, and simultaneously extremely difficult to evaluate in studies, that it is hard to know how to assess any claims made about it. In 2022, American model Hailey Bieber (wife of singer Justin) said about a vitamin infusion containing the molecule nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD): ‘I’m going to NAD for the rest of my life and never going to age.’
